Moderate/ severe depression responds best to a combination of antidepressants and counseling. This study will estimate the proportion of women who return to functionality after treatment with Desvenlafaxine and examine the differential impact of change in depression and anxiety sympt

literature.title: A Comprehensive Review on Postpartum Depression.
literature.abstract: One of the most common psychological effects following childbirth is postpartum depression. Postpartum depression (PPD) has a significant negative impact on the child's emotional, mental as well as intellectual development if left untreated, which can later have long-term complications. Later in life, it also results in the mother developing obsessive-compulsive disorder and anxiety. Many psychological risk factors are linked with PPD. literature.title: A double blind comparison of venlafaxine and paroxetine in obsessive-compulsive disorder.
authors: van Megen Harold J G M
literature.abstract: While the usefulness of clomipramine and selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors (SSRIs) in obsessive-compulsive disorder (OCD) has been established, the efficacy of serotonin-norepinephrine reuptake inhibitors remains to be determined. This report describes the first randomized double-blind comparison study of an SNRI in patients with obsessive-compulsive disorder. literature.title: An updated review of antidepressants with marked serotonergic effects in obsessive-compulsive disorder.
literature.abstract: Since the recognition of the effectiveness of clomipramine in treating obsessive-compulsive disorder (OCD), a number of recent empirical studies have confirmed a key role of the serotonergic (5-HT) system in the pathophysiology of OCD. The current study presents a review of the existing double-blind studies testing 5-HT antidepressants in OCD.

literature.title: Risperidone Augmentation in Antidepressant-Resistant Somatic Symptom Disorder.

Risperidone is an effective augmenting agent for treatment-resistant major depressive and obsessive-compulsive disorders. Although various antidepressants have been used for the pharmacotherapy of SSDs, no guidelines have been formulated for treatment-resistant or severe SSDs. clinical_trials.title: eIMPACT-DM Pilot Trial: Depression Treatment to Reduce the Excess Diabetes Risk of People With Depression and Prediabetes
clinical_trials.brief_summary: This pilot randomized controlled trial seeks: (1) to determine the preliminary efficacy of our modernized collaborative care intervention for depression in improving the diabetes risk markers of hemoglobin A1c and insulin resistance and (2) to explore whether somatic depressive symptoms - i.e., hyperphagia (increased appetite/weight) and/or hypersomnia (increased sleep) - moderate the effect of the eIMPACT-DM intervention on diabetes risk markers.

relevance.reasoning: eIMPACT-DM Phase 2 研究探討憂鬱症治療降低糖尿病風險（n=46），納入持續性憂鬱症患者，Desvenlafaxine 非唯一研究藥物，間接相關。

clinical_trials.title: An 8-week Open-Label Flexible-Dose Study Of Desvenlafaxine as Monotherapy In The Treatment Of Dysthymia
clinical_trials.brief_summary: This multi-centred study will be conducted at two centres. The design will be an open label, flexible-dose study. This investigation will evaluate the efficacy of Desvenlafaxine monotherapy for patients who meet diagnostic criteria for dysthymia.

relevance.reasoning: 【最直接相關】Desvenlafaxine 單藥治療 Dysthymia 的 8 週開放標籤彈性劑量研究（n=30），已完成。雖非 RCT 設計（Phase NA），為迄今針對此確切適應症的直接介入試驗。

clinical_trials.title: Desvenlafaxine (Pristiq) vs. Placebo in the Treatment of Chronic Depression
clinical_trials.brief_summary:
The investigators are studying a new antidepressant medicine, desvenlafaxine, for the treatment of people with chronic depression. Desvenlafaxine (trade name Pristiq) has been approved by the FDA for the treatment of major depression.

The investigators are testing whether this medicine is also effective for adults with a type of chronic depression that is less severe than major depression. This condition is also known as dysthymic disorder or dysthymia. Chronic depression, lasting two or more y

relevance.reasoning: 【最強臨床證據】Phase 4 Desvenlafaxine（Pristiq）vs 安慰劑用於慢性憂鬱症 RCT（n=59），已完成。直接對比安慰劑設計，為本適應症提供最高質量的隨機對照試驗數據。

literature.title: Efficacy of antidepressants for dysthymia: a meta-analysis of placebo-controlled randomized trials.
literature.abstract: The authors sought to determine the efficacy of antidepressants in dysthymic disorder and to compare antidepressant and placebo response rates between major depressive disorder (MDD) and dysthymic disorder.

literature.title: Do social functioning and symptoms improve with continuation antidepressant treatment of persistent depressive disorder? An observational study.
literature.abstract: To determine efficacy of continued treatment with the serotonin norepinephrine reuptake inhibitor duloxetine on symptom reduction and functional improvement in outpatients with dysthymia.

repurposing_rationale.mechanistic_link: 持續性憂鬱症（慢性輕鬱症）與 MDD 共享部分神經生物學基礎，包含單胺類神經傳遞功能不足。Desvenlafaxine 作為 SNRI 具備直接機轉適用性，且已有 Phase 4 RCT（NCT01537068）直接測試 Desvenlafaxine vs 安慰劑於慢性憂鬱症，以及開放標籤 Dysthymia 專項研究（NCT01948895），屬目前分析中臨床證據最充分的新適應症之一。
雖 SNRI 在恐慌症及廣泛性焦慮症有一定療效，廣場恐懼症通常作為恐慌症的共病處理，但無直接 Desvenlafaxine 臨床證據。在無任何試驗或文獻支持下，目前僅為計算預測，需先建立研究問題。

There will be three visits for depressed patients and two for healthy controls (the first and third visits). relevance.reasoning: Phase 4 研究探討 MDD 患者治療對決策能力影響（n=53），Desvenlafaxine 為治療藥物，主要結果為神經認知功能而非憂鬱症狀評分，且未區分 Melancholia 亞型。間接支持 Desvenlafaxine 於 MDD 的耐受性。

literature.title: Comparative efficacy and acceptability of antidepressants, psychotherapies, and their combination for acute treatment of children and adolescents with depressive disorder: a systematic review and network meta-analysis.
literature.abstract: Depressive disorders are common in children and adolescents. Antidepressants, psychotherapies, and their combination are often used in routine clinical practice; however, available evidence on the comparative efficacy and safety of these interventions is inconclusive. Therefore, we sought to compare and rank all available treatment interventions for the acute treatment of depressive disorders in children and adolescents.

literature.title: New generation antidepressants for depression in children and adolescents: a network meta-analysis.
literature.journal: The Cochrane database of systematic reviews
literature.abstract: Major depressive disorders have a significant impact on children and adolescents, including on educational and vocational outcomes, interpersonal relationships, and physical and mental health and well-being. There is an association between major depressive disorder and suicidal ideation, suicide attempts, and suicide. Antidepressant medication is used in moderate to severe depression; there is now a range of newer generations of these medications.

literature.title: Gastrointestinal side effects associated with antidepressant treatments in patients with major depressive disorder: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
literature.abstract: Gastrointestinal side effects (SEs) are frequently observed in patients with major depressive disorder (MDD) while taking antidepressants and may lead to treatment discontinuation. The aim of this meta-analysis is to provide quantitative measures on short-term rates of gastrointestinal SEs in MDD patients treated with second-generation antidepressants. An electronic search of the literature was conducted by using MEDLINE, ISI Web of Science - Web of Science Core Collection, and Cochrane Library

literature.title: The effects of antidepressants on cardiometabolic and other physiological parameters: a systematic review and network meta-analysis.
literature.abstract: Antidepressants induce physiological alterations; however, the degree to which these occur in treatment with various antidepressants is unclear. We aimed to compare and rank antidepressants based on physiological side-effects by synthesising data from randomised controlled trials (RCTs).

literature.title: Efficacy and tolerability of desvenlafaxine in the real-world treatment of patients with major depression: a narrative review and an expert opinion paper.
literature.abstract: Major depressive disorder (MDD) is a common severe mental disorder, requiring a tailored and integrated treatment. Several approaches are available including different classes of antidepressants various psychotherapeutic approaches, and psychosocial interventions. The treatment plan for each patient with MDD should be differentiated on the basis of several clinical, personal, and contextual factors.

literature.title: Antidepressants for depression in stage 3-5 chronic kidney disease: a systematic review of pharmacokinetics, efficacy and safety with recommendations by European Renal Best Practice (ERBP).

literature.title: Efficacy of Desvenlafaxine Compared With Placebo in Major Depressive Disorder Patients by Age Group and Severity of Depression at Baseline.
literature.abstract: This post hoc meta-analysis evaluated the efficacy and safety of desvenlafaxine 50 and 100 mg versus placebo across age groups and severity of depression at baseline in patients with major depressive disorder.

literature.title: Esketamine Combined With SSRI or SNRI for Treatment-Resistant Depression.
literature.abstract: Treatment-resistant depression (TRD) remains a critical challenge in psychiatry, with limited effective options. Esketamine, a rapid-acting antidepressant, is usually combined with a selective serotonin reuptake inhibitor (SSRI) or a serotonin-norepinephrine reuptake inhibitor (SNRI), but comparative evidence of these combinations' effectiveness in real-world settings is sparse.

literature.title: Desvenlafaxine succinate: a newer antidepressant for the treatment of depression and somatic symptoms.
literature.abstract: Desvenlafaxine succinate (DVS) is one of several serotonin-norepinephrine reuptake inhibitors (SNRIs). Others are venlafaxine hydrochloride, milnacipran, and duloxetine. literature.title: Efficacy and Safety of Escitalopram, Desvenlafaxine, and Vortioxetine in the Acute Treatment of Anxious Depression: A Randomized Rater-blinded 6-week Clinical Trial.
literature.journal: Clinical psychopharmacology and neuroscience : the official scientific journal of the Korean College of Neuropsychopharmacology
literature.abstract: Anxious depression is associated with greater chronicity, higher severity of symptoms, more severe functional impairment, and poor response to drug treatment. However, evidence for first-choice antidepressants in patients with anxious depression is limited. This study aimed to compare the efficacy and safety of escitalopram, desvenlafaxine, and vortioxetine in the acute treatment of anxious depression.

literature.title: Desvenlafaxine: another "me too" drug?
literature.abstract: To compare desvenlafaxine with its parent drug, venlafaxine, to determine the usefulness of this new medication.

literature.title: Desvenlafaxine: a new antidepressant or just another one?

It was approved in February 2008 by the United States Food and Drug Administration for the treatment of major depressive disorder (MDD) based on a number of randomized, placebo-controlled clinical trials demonstrating efficacy and safety for patients with MDD. literature.title: Speed of Improvement in Symptoms of Depression With Desvenlafaxine 50 mg and 100 mg Compared With Placebo in Patients With Major Depressive Disorder.
literature.abstract: This post hoc analysis examined the time point at which clinically significant improvement in major depressive disorder (MDD) symptoms occurs with desvenlafaxine versus placebo.

literature.title: Acute Efficacy and Safety of Escitalopram Versus Desvenlafaxine and Vortioxetine in the Treatment of Depression With Cognitive Complaint: A Rater-Blinded Randomized Comparative Study.
literature.abstract: This study aimed to compare the efficacy and safety of escitalopram, vortioxetine, and desvenlafaxine for acute treatment of major depressive disorder (MDD) with cognitive complaint (CC).

literature.title: Desvenlafaxine Versus Placebo in the Treatment of Children and Adolescents with Major Depressive Disorder.

literature.abstract: To evaluate the short-term efficacy and safety of desvenlafaxine versus placebo in the treatment of children and adolescents with major depressive disorder (MDD).

repurposing_rationale.mechanistic_link: 憂鬱型憂鬱症（Melancholia）為 MDD 嚴重亞型，以顯著快感缺失、精神運動遲滯、晨間惡化為特徵，需較強 NE 再回收抑制，Desvenlafaxine 的雙重 SNRI 機轉理論上具備適應性。Desvenlafaxine 已在 MDD 累積充分證據（PMID 26895080 整合分析；PMID 37450377 真實世界研究），但無專針對 Melancholia 亞型的 Phase 3 RCT。注意：Melancholia 非獨立 ICD 診斷碼，為 MDD 嚴重度標記。
